ctx.x: A few days after we arrived I was contacted to make a five days tour with a small variety show called Radio Cocktail 51. The three Peter Sisters who were a very popular singing trio in the States were in France and there were two younger sisters named Edith and Joyce who had formed a singing duo and they were part of the show which included André Salvador, the brother of Henri who was very famous singer and comedian in Europe. I first met the Salvador brothers in late 1935 at the Villa d'Este when they were about…

The two sisters were billed as the Peter Sisters Jr. and their mother travelled with us. Our first date was in Perpignan at the Nouveau theatre the 23rd of October. Then came Toulouse, Castre, Montpellier, Beziers, which was the last date. In Montpellier, Joyce and Edith ran into some racial trouble which I have never experienced in France. They had been booked in a different hotel from the one we were in and when they arrived and asked for their reservations, they were told that none had been made for them. Miss…

We came back to Paris the 28th of October and did different gigs the 11th of November when Don Byas and myself were engaged to open a new club called the Perroquet. A Hollywood starlet named Marsha Gayle was the directorist of the club which was at 49, rue de Ponthieu in back of the Champs Elysees. Ruddy Castel, a cuban orchestra leader played afro-cuban music while Don and I taken care of the jazz.
